# SUPPLY AGREEMENT

This Supply Agreement (this "**Agreement**") is entered into and made effective as of March 1, 2024 (the "**Supply Agreement Effective Date**" or the "**Effective Date**") by and between:

**Veltmar Glassworks, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 1400 Furnace Road, Wilmington, Delaware 19801 ("**Supplier**"); and

**Harrowgate Bottling Co.**, a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 220 Millrace Avenue, Harrisburg, Pennsylvania 17101 ("**Customer**").

Supplier and Customer are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

A. Supplier manufactures glass and other beverage containers.

B. Customer bottles and distributes beverage products and wishes to buy containers from Supplier.

C. The Parties wish to set out the terms on which Supplier will supply, and Customer will buy, those containers.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants in this Agreement and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 "**Affiliate**" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a Party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting equity of the entity.

1.2 "**Containers**" means bottles, jars and other containers for holding beverage products, together with associated closures where supplied by Supplier.

1.3 "**Products**" means the Containers listed in Exhibit A, as updated by the Parties in writing from time to time.

1.4 "**Purchase Order**" means a written order for Products issued by Customer under this Agreement.

1.5 "**Price Adjustment Notice**" has the meaning given in Section 5.3.

1.6 "**Quality Agreement**" means the Quality and Specifications Agreement between Supplier and Customer, as amended from time to time.

1.7 "**Specifications**" means the specifications for each Product set out in Exhibit A and in the Quality Agreement.

1.8 "**Term**" means the Initial Term together with any Renewal Terms.

1.9 "**Recall**" has the meaning given in Section 10.1.

## 2. TERM

2.1 **Initial Term.** The initial term of this Agreement shall be three years from the Supply Agreement Effective Date (the "**Initial Term**"), unless terminated earlier under Section 13.

2.2 **Renewal.** At the end of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive five-year Renewal Terms, five years each (each, a "**Renewal Term**"), unless either Party gives the other written notice of non-renewal not more than 270 days and not less than 240 days before the expiration of the Initial Term or the then-current Renewal Term. All terms of this Agreement, including Sections 3 and 5, continue to apply during each Renewal Term.

## 3. EXCLUSIVITY AND FORECASTS

3.1 **Exclusive Purchase.** During the Term, Customer shall purchase from Supplier, and Supplier shall be Customer's exclusive source of, all glass and PET containers for any beverage product manufactured, filled, bottled or packaged by or for Customer or its Affiliates, worldwide. Customer shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, purchase any such containers from any third party during the Term.

3.2 **Forecasts.** By the fifteenth (15th) day of each calendar month, Customer shall provide Supplier with a rolling twelve (12) month non-binding forecast of its expected Product requirements by Product and delivery location. The first three (3) months of each forecast are firm and binding on Customer.

3.3 **Capacity.** Supplier shall maintain production capacity sufficient to meet one hundred fifteen percent (115%) of Customer's most recent forecast. Supplier shall notify Customer promptly if it anticipates any shortfall in its ability to supply.

## 4. ORDERS AND DELIVERY

4.1 **Purchase Orders.** Customer shall order Products by Purchase Order at least thirty (30) days before the requested delivery date. Supplier shall accept or reject each Purchase Order within five (5) business days of receipt. Supplier shall not reject a Purchase Order that is consistent with the firm portion of Customer's forecast.

4.2 **Terms Governing Orders.** This Agreement governs each Purchase Order. Any additional or conflicting terms in a Purchase Order, acknowledgment, invoice or other ordering document have no effect.

4.3 **Delivery.** Supplier shall deliver Products FCA Supplier's facility (Incoterms 2020) to the carrier designated by Customer, unless the Purchase Order specifies otherwise. Supplier shall deliver Products on the delivery date stated in the accepted Purchase Order.

4.4 **Title and Risk.** Title to and risk of loss of the Products pass to Customer on delivery in accordance with Section 4.3.

4.5 **Late Delivery.** If Supplier fails to deliver any Products within five (5) business days after the agreed delivery date, Customer may, in addition to its other remedies, cancel the affected portion of the Purchase Order without liability.

## 5. PRICING AND PAYMENT

5.1 **Prices.** Customer shall pay the prices for the Products set out in Exhibit B, as adjusted under this Section 5.

5.2 **Invoicing and Payment.** Supplier shall invoice Customer on shipment. Customer shall pay undisputed invoices within forty-five (45) days of receipt. Customer may withhold any amount it disputes in good faith, provided it notifies Supplier of the dispute and the reasons for it before the due date.

5.3 **Price Adjustments.** Supplier may adjust the prices in Exhibit B not more than once in any twelve (12) month period by giving Customer written notice of the adjustment, the effective date of the adjustment and reasonable supporting detail of the cost changes on which it is based (a "**Price Adjustment Notice**"). No price adjustment shall take effect earlier than sixty (60) days after Customer's receipt of the Price Adjustment Notice.

5.4 **Objection.** Cu

If Customer objects in time, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith for thirty (30) days, and the existing prices shall remain in effect during that period. If the Parties do not agree within that period, either Party may refer the matter for resolution under Section 15.6. Any price adjustment to which Customer does not object within the period stated in this Section 5.4 is deemed accepted by Customer and takes effect on the date stated in the Price Adjustment Notice.

5.5 **Taxes.** Prices are exclusive of sales, use and similar taxes, which Customer shall pay unless Customer provides a valid exemption certificate. Each Party is responsible for taxes on its own income.

## 6. QUALITY AND SPECIFICATIONS

6.1 **Specifications.** Supplier shall manufacture all Products in accordance with the Specifications, the Quality Agreement and all applicable laws, including laws governing materials in contact with food and beverages.

6.2 **Quality Agreement.** The Parties shall comply with the Quality Agreement, which governs inspection, testing, quality control, change control and related matters.

6.3 **Changes.** Supplier shall not change any raw material, process, mold, facility or Specification affecting the Products without Customer's prior written consent.

## 7. INSPECTION AND ACCEPTANCE

7.1 **Inspection.** Customer may inspect the Products within thirty (30) days after delivery. Customer may reject any Products that do not conform to the Specifications by notice to Supplier describing the nonconformity.

7.2 **Rejected Products.** At Customer's option, Supplier shall promptly replace rejected Products or credit Customer for them, and shall bear the cost of returning or disposing of rejected Products. Acceptance of Products does not waive any warranty or other right of Customer.

## 8. WARRANTIES

8.1 **Product Warranty.** Supplier warrants that, for eighteen (18) months after delivery, the Products will (a) conform to the Specifications; (b) be free from defects in materials and workmanship; (c) be fit for holding and distributing beverage products; and (d) comply with all applicable laws.

8.2 **Title and Non-Infringement.** Supplier warrants that it will convey good title to the Products free of all liens, and that the Products and their manufacture do not infringe any third party's intellectual property rights.

8.3 **Mutual Warranties.** Each Party warrants that it is duly organized and in good standing, and that it has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement.

8.4 **Disclaimer.** EXCEPT AS SET OUT IN THIS SECTION 8, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY OTHER WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED.

## 9. INDEMNIFICATION

9.1 **By Supplier.** Supplier shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates and their officers, directors, employees and agents from and against all losses, damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising from any third-party claim to the extent arising out of (a) any defect in, or nonconformity of, the Products; (b) any personal injury, death or property damage caused by the Products; (c) any claim that the Products infringe a third party's intellectual property rights; or (d) Supplier's breach of this Agreement, negligence or willful misconduct.

9.2 **By Customer.** Customer shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Supplier and its officers, directors, employees and agents from and against all losses, damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising from any third-party claim to the extent arising out of the beverage contents filled into the Products by Customer, or Customer's negligence or willful misconduct.

9.3 **Procedure.** The indemnified Party shall notify the indemnifying Party promptly of any claim, allow the indemnifying Party to control its defense and settlement, and cooperate reasonably at the indemnifying Party's expense. The indemnifying Party shall not settle any claim in a way that imposes any obligation on, or admits fault by, the indemnified Party without its prior written consent.

## 10. RECALLS

10.1 **Recall Events.** If any governmental authority requires, or Customer reasonably determines it necessary, to recall, withdraw or correct any beverage product filled in the Products because of a defect in or nonconformity of the Products (a "**Recall**"), Customer shall notify Supplier and the Parties shall cooperate in carrying out the Recall.

10.2 **Recall Costs.** Supplier shall reimburse Customer for all reasonable costs and expenses of any Recall to the extent caused by a defect in or nonconformity of the Products. These costs include notification, retrieval, transport, storage and destruction costs, the cost of replacement Products and lost beverage contents, and customer credits and refunds.

10.3 **Records.** Supplier shall maintain lot and batch traceability records for all Products for at least five (5) years after delivery and shall provide them to Customer on request.

## 11. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

11.1 **Cap.** Except as provided in Section 11.2, each Party's total liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement, whether in contract, tort or otherwise, shall not exceed the fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.

11.2 **Exclusions.** The limitation in Section 11.1 and the exclusion in Section 11.3 do not apply to (a) Supplier's indemnity obligations under Section 9.1; (b) Recall costs under Section 10; (c) either Party's breach of Section 12; or (d) a Party's gross negligence, fraud or willful misconduct.

11.3 **Consequential Damages.** Except as provided in Section 11.2, neither Party is liable for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages, or for lost profits, arising out of or relating to this Agreement.

## 12. CO

NFIDENTIALITY

12.1 **Obligations.** Each Party shall keep confidential all non-public business, technical and financial information disclosed by the other Party in connection with this Agreement ("**Confidential Information**"), and shall use it only to perform this Agreement. Each Party may disclose Confidential Information to its employees, Affiliates and advisers who need to know it and are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as this Section 12.

12.2 **Exceptions.** Confidential Information does not include information that (a) is or becomes public other than through the receiving Party's breach; (b) was known to the receiving Party without restriction before disclosure; (c) is independently developed by the receiving Party; or (d) is lawfully received from a third party without restriction. A Party may disclose Confidential Information as required by law, after giving the other Party prompt notice where lawful.

12.3 **Duration.** The obligations in this Section 12 continue during the Term and for five (5) years after its end.

## 13. TERMINATION

13.1 **For Breach.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement by written notice if the other Party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure the breach within thirty (30) days after receiving notice of it.

13.2 **Insolvency.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement immediately by written notice if the other Party becomes insolvent, makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors, has a receiver appointed, or becomes the subject of any bankruptcy proceeding that is not dismissed within sixty (60) days.

13.3 **Effect.** On termination or expiration, Supplier shall fulfil all accepted Purchase Orders unless Customer instructs otherwise, and Customer shall pay for all Products delivered. Sections 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13.3 and 15 survive termination or expiration.

## 14. GENERAL OBLIGATIONS AND ASSIGNMENT

14.1 **Insurance.** During the Term and for three (3) years after its end, Supplier shall maintain commercial general liability insurance, including products liability and product recall coverage, with limits of not less than $10,000,000 per occurrence, and shall name Customer as an additional insured.

14.2 **Compliance.** Each Party shall comply with all laws applicable to its performance of this Agreement.

14.3 **Assignment.** Neither Party may assign or transfer this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations under it, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other Party. Any attempted assignment in violation of this Section 14.3 is void. This Agreement binds and benefits the Parties and their permitted successors and assigns.

## 15. MISCELLANEOUS

15.1 **Entire Agreement.** This Agreement, together with its Exhibits and the Quality Agreement, is the entire agreement of the Parties on its subject matter and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous negotiations, term sheets, proposals, understandings and agreements, written or oral, on that subject matter.

15.2 **Order of Precedence.** If there is any conflict among the documents governing the Parties' relationship, they control in the following order: written amendments, then Supply Agreement, then Quality Agreement.

15.3 **Amendment and Waiver.** This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by both Parties. No waiver is effective unless it is in writing and signed by the waiving Party.

15.4 **Notices.** All notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier or by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the addresses stated at the beginning of this Agreement (or another address a Party designates by notice). Notices are effective on receipt.

15.5 **Governing Law.** This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply.

15.6 **Dispute Resolution.** The Parties shall first attempt to resolve any dispute through good-faith negotiation between senior executives for thirty (30) days. If the dispute is not resolved, either Party may bring proceedings in the state or federal courts located in Wilmington, Delaware, and each Party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of those courts.

15.7 **Force Majeure.** Neither Party is liable for a delay or failure in performance caused by events beyond its reasonable control, other than payment obligations, provided it notifies the other Party promptly and uses reasonable efforts to resume performance. If a force majeure event affecting Supplier continues for more than thirty (30) days, Customer may buy affected Products from third parties for the duration of the event without breaching Section 3.1.

15.8 **Relationship.** The Parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture or agency relationship.

15.9 **Severability.** If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain in full force and effect.

15.10 **Counterparts.** This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together are one instrument.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Agreement as of the Supply Agreement Effective Date.

**VELTMAR GLASSWORKS, INC.**

# AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO SUPPLY AGREEMENT

This Amendment No. 1 to Supply Agreement (this "**Amendment**") is entered into as of September 21, 2026 (the "**Amendment Date**") by and between:

**Veltmar Glassworks, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 1400 Furnace Road, Wilmington, Delaware 19801 ("**Supplier**"); and

**Harrowgate Bottling Co.**, a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 220 Millrace Avenue, Harrisburg, Pennsylvania 17101 ("**Customer**").

Supplier and Customer are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

A. Supplier and Customer are parties to a Supply Agreement made effective as of March 1, 2024 (the "**Agreement**"), under which Supplier supplies, and Customer purchases, beverage containers.

B. Section 15.3 of the Agreement provides that the Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by both Parties.

C. Under Section 5.3 of the Agreement, Supplier issued a Price Adjustment Notice dated July 30, 2026. The notice provides for an increase of fourteen percent (14%) in the prices set out in Exhibit B to the Agreement, effective October 2, 2026, and it was received by Customer on August 3, 2026. No objection to the Price Adjustment Notice has been delivered by Customer, and the Price Adjustment Notice remains subject to Section 5.4 of the Agreement.

D. The Parties wish to clarify and amend certain provisions of the Agreement as set out in this Amendment.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants in this Amendment and in the Agreement, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

1.1 **Defined Terms.** Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Amendment have the meanings given to them in the Agreement.

1.2 **References.** On and after the Amendment Date, each reference in the Agreement to "this Agreement," "hereunder," "hereof" or words of similar meaning means the Agreement as amended by this Amendment.

## 2. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

2.1 Section 11.2 of the Agreement is deleted in its entirety and replaced with the following:

> "11.2 **Exclusions.** The limitation in Section 11.1 and the exclusion in Section 11.3 do not apply to (a) Supplier's indemnity obligations under Section 9.1, which are excluded solely to third-party intellectual property claims under Section 9.1(c); (b) either Party's breach of Section 12; or (c) a Party's gross negligence, fraud or willful misconduct."

2.2 The amended Section 11.2 applies to all claims arising on or after the Amendment Date.

## 3. NOTICES

3.1 Section 15.4 of the Agreement is amended by adding the following at the end of that Section:

> "A copy of each notice to Supplier must also be sent to: Veltmar Glassworks, Inc., Attention: General Counsel, 1400 Furnace Road, Wilmington, Delaware 19801. A copy of each notice to Customer must also be sent to: Harrowgate Bottling Co., Attention: Legal Department, 220 Millrace Avenue, Harrisburg, Pennsylvania 17101. Failure to send a copy does not affect the effectiveness of a notice otherwise given in accordance with this Section 15.4."

## 4. ASSIGNMENT

4.1 Section 14 of the Agreement is amended by adding the following new Section 14.4 immediately after Section 14.3:

> "14.4 **Assignment by Supplier.** Notwithstanding Section 14.3, Supplier may assign or transfer this Agreement, in whole or in part, or any of its rights or obligations under it, without the consent of Customer, to (a) any Affiliate of Supplier; or (b) any successor to Supplier by merger, consolidation, change of control or sale of all or substantially all of the business or assets of Supplier to which this Agreement relates. Supplier shall give Customer written notice of any such assignment within thirty (30) days after it takes effect."

## 5. EFFECT OF AMENDMENT

5.1 **Ratification.** Except as expressly amended by this Amendment, the Agreement remains unchanged and in full force and effect, and is ratified and confirmed by the Parties.

5.2 **Written Amendment.** This Amendment is a written amendment for the purposes of Sections 15.2 and 15.3 of the Agreement.

5.3 **No Other Waiver.** Nothing in this Amendment operates as a waiver of any right, power or remedy of either Party under the Agreement, except as expressly set out in this Amendment.

## 6. GENERAL

6.1 **Governing Law.** This Amendment is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules.

6.2 **Dispute Resolution.** Section 15.6 of the Agreement applies to any dispute arising out of or relating to this Amendment.

6.3 **Counterparts.** This Amendment may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature. Each counterpart is an original, and all counterparts together are one instrument.

6.4 **Authority.** Each Party represents that the individual signing this Amendment on its behalf is duly authorized to do so.

# TERM SHEET

**Proposed Supply Arrangement for Beverage Containers**

**Date:** January 22, 2024

**Between:** Veltmar Glassworks, Inc. ("**Supplier**") and Harrowgate Bottling Co. ("**Customer**")

This term sheet summarizes the principal terms the parties have discussed for the supply of beverage containers by Supplier to Customer. Except for Sections 10 and 11, this term sheet is not binding on either party. It does not create an obligation to negotiate or to enter into a definitive agreement. Binding obligations will arise only under a definitive supply agreement signed by both parties (the "**Definitive Agreement**").

## 1. Products

1.1 Supplier will manufacture and supply glass beverage containers to Customer. The initial products are:

| Item | Product | Capacity | Color |
|---|---|---|---|
| A-1 | Long-neck beer bottle | 12 fl. oz. | Amber |
| A-2 | Long-neck beer bottle | 22 fl. oz. | Amber |
| A-3 | Stubby beer bottle | 11.2 fl. oz. | Amber |

1.2 Detailed specifications will be set out in a separate quality and specifications agreement to be entered into between the parties.

## 2. Exclusivity

2.1 During the term, Supplier will be Customer's exclusive supplier of amber glass bottles for Customer's beer brands at its U.S. and Canadian facilities.

2.2 Customer remains free to source from any supplier all other containers, including containers for non-beer products, containers made from materials other than amber glass, and containers for facilities outside the United States and Canada.

2.3 If Supplier cannot supply because of a force majeure event lasting more than thirty (30) days, Customer may buy affected products from third parties for the duration of the event.

## 3. Term

3.1 The initial term will be three (3) years from the effective date of the Definitive Agreement.

3.2 Any renewal mechanics will be negotiated in the Definitive Agreement.

## 4. Forecasts and Orders

4.1 Customer will provide a monthly rolling twelve (12) month forecast. The first three (3) months of each forecast will be binding.

4.2 Supplier will maintain capacity to meet one hundred fifteen percent (115%) of Customer's most recent forecast.

4.3 Customer will place purchase orders at least thirty (30) days before the requested delivery date. Delivery will be FCA Supplier's facility (Incoterms 2020).

## 5. Pricing and Payment

5.1 Initial pricing per gross (144 units):

| Item | Price per Gross | Minimum Order |
|---|---|---|
| A-1 | $38.40 | 500 gross |
| A-2 | $61.20 | 250 gross |
| A-3 | $36.10 | 500 gross |

5.2 Supplier may adjust prices no more than once in any twelve (12) month period. Supplier must give written notice with supporting cost detail. No adjustment will take effect earlier than sixty (60) days after Customer receives the notice.

5.3 Customer may object to a price adjustment within thirty (30) days after receiving the notice. The parties will then negotiate in good faith, and existing prices will apply during the negotiation.

5.4 Payment of undisputed invoices will be due within forty-five (45) days of receipt.

## 6. Quality, Warranty and Recalls

6.1 Supplier will warrant, for eighteen (18) months after delivery, that the products conform to specifications, are free from defects and are fit for holding and distributing beverage products.

6.2 Supplier will reimburse Customer for the reasonable costs of any recall to the extent caused by a defect in or nonconformity of the products.

6.3 Supplier will maintain product liability and product recall insurance of not less than $10,000,000 per occurrence and will name Customer as an additional insured.

## 7. Indemnities and Liability

7.1 Supplier will indemnify Customer against third-party claims arising from product defects, personal injury or property damage caused by the products, intellectual property infringement, and Supplier's breach, negligence or willful misconduct. Customer will indemnify Supplier against third-party claims arising from the beverage contents and Customer's negligence or willful misconduct.

7.2 Each party's liability will be capped at the fees paid by Customer in the six (6) months before the claim arose. The cap will not apply to Supplier's indemnity obligations, recall costs, breaches of confidentiality, or gross negligence, fraud or willful misconduct.

## 8. Assignment

8.1 Neither party may assign the Definitive Agreement without the prior written consent of the other party.

## 9. Governing Law

9.1 The Definitive Agreement will be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware.

## 10. Confidentiality (Binding)

10.1 Each party will keep the terms of this term sheet, and all non-public information exchanged in connection with it, confidential. This Section 10 survives for two (2) years from the date of this term sheet.

## 11. Costs (Binding)

11.1 Each party will bear its own costs and expenses relating to this term sheet and the negotiation of the Definitive Agreement.

# QUALITY AND SPECIFICATIONS AGREEMENT

This Quality and Specifications Agreement (this "**Quality Agreement**") is entered into and made effective as of March 1, 2024 (the "**Effective Date**") by and between:

**Veltmar Glassworks, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 1400 Furnace Road, Wilmington, Delaware 19801 ("**Supplier**"); and

**Harrowgate Bottling Co.**, a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 220 Millrace Avenue, Harrisburg, Pennsylvania 17101 ("**Customer**").

Supplier and Customer are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

A. Supplier and Customer are parties to a Supply Agreement made effective as of March 1, 2024 (the "**Supply Agreement**"), under which Supplier supplies, and Customer purchases, the Products.

B. Section 6.2 of the Supply Agreement provides that the Parties shall comply with this Quality Agreement, which governs inspection, testing, quality control, change control and related matters.

C. The Parties wish to set out the Specifications for the Products and the quality requirements that apply to their manufacture, testing, release and delivery.

NOW, THEREFORE, the Parties agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

1.1 **Defined Terms.** Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Quality Agreement have the meanings given to them in the Supply Agreement.

1.2 **Additional Definitions.** In this Quality Agreement:

(a) "**Certificate of Analysis**" or "**CoA**" means a document issued by Supplier for each Lot confirming that the Lot has been tested and conforms to the Specifications.

(b) "**Critical Defect**" means a defect that is likely to cause injury to a consumer or render the Product unusable for filling, including glass inclusions, internal glass particles, sharp edges, birdswings and cracked finishes.

(c) "**Lot**" means a quantity of a single Product manufactured on the same production line during a single continuous production run and identified by a unique lot number.

(d) "**Major Defect**" means a defect, other than a Critical Defect, that is likely to cause a failure on Customer's filling or packaging lines or materially impair the appearance or performance of the Product.

(e) "**Nonconformance**" means any failure of a Product or Lot to conform to the Specifications or to this Quality Agreement.

1.3 **Relationship to Supply Agreement.** This Quality Agreement supplements the Supply Agreement. The order of precedence set out in Section 15.2 of the Supply Agreement applies to this Quality Agreement.

## 2. SPECIFICATIONS

2.1 **Product Specifications.** Supplier shall manufacture each Product in accordance with the specification referenced for that Product in Exhibit A to the Supply Agreement, as set out in Schedule 1 to this Quality Agreement.

2.2 **Food-Contact Compliance.** Supplier shall ensure that all Products, and all materials, coatings and treatments used in their manufacture, comply with applicable laws governing materials in contact with food and beverages, including 21 C.F.R. Parts 174 to 186 and, for Products delivered to facilities in Canada, the Food and Drugs Act (Canada) and its regulations.

2.3 **Updates.** Specifications may be updated only by a written document signed by an authorized quality representative of each Party. Any updated Specification takes effect on the date stated in that document.

## 3. QUALITY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM

3.1 **Certification.** Supplier shall maintain throughout the Term a quality management system certified to ISO 9001:2015 and a food safety management system certified under a scheme recognized by the Global Food Safety Initiative (GFSI) for packaging manufacture, and shall provide current certificates to Customer on request.

3.2 **Quality Representatives.** Each Party shall appoint a quality representative responsible for matters under this Quality Agreement and shall notify the other Party of any change of representative.

3.3 **Personnel and Hygiene.** Supplier shall ensure that personnel involved in manufacturing, inspecting and packing the Products are trained in good manufacturing practices and hygiene appropriate to food-contact packaging.

## 4. MANUFACTURING CONTROLS AND TESTING

4.1 **In-Process Controls.** Supplier shall operate automated inspection equipment on each production line capable of detecting dimensional, finish and glass-integrity defects, and shall maintain documented sampling and inspection plans for each Product.

4.2 **Release Testing.** Before releasing any Lot for delivery, Supplier shall test the Lot for the parameters stated in Schedule 1, including dimensions, capacity, internal pressure resistance, thermal shock resistance and color transmission.

4.3 **Acceptable Quality Levels.** Supplier shall release a Lot only if it meets the following acceptable quality levels (AQL) under ANSI/ASQ Z1.4, General Inspection Level II:

| Defect Classification | AQL |
|---|---|
| Critical Defect | 0.0 (zero tolerance) |
| Major Defect | 0.65 |
| Minor Defect | 2.5 |

4.4 **Certificates of Analysis.** Supplier shall provide a CoA for each Lot with, or before, delivery of that Lot.

## 5. PACKAGING, LABELING AND TRACEABILITY

5.1 **Packaging.** Supplier shall palletize Products in clean, dry, shrink-wrapped bulk pallets with tier sheets and top frames suitable for automated depalletizing, protected from dust, moisture and foreign matter.

5.2 **Labeling.** Each pallet shall bear a label stating the Product item number, quantity, Lot number, production date, production line and Supplier facility.

5.3 **Traceability.** Supplier shall maintain lot and batch traceability for all Products in accordance with Section 10.3 of the Supply Agreement, so that each Lot can be traced to its raw materials, production line and production date, and to the delivery in which it was shipped.

## 6. INSPECTION AND NONCONFORMANCE

6.1 **Incoming Inspection.** Customer may inspect and test Products

quality_agreement.md, page 2 of 3:
 after delivery within the period set out in Section 7.1 of the Supply Agreement. Supplier's release of a Lot does not limit Customer's rights under Sections 7 and 8 of the Supply Agreement.

6.2 **Nonconformance Notice.** If Customer identifies a Nonconformance, it shall notify Supplier's quality representative, identifying the affected Product and Lot and describing the Nonconformance. Where reasonably available, Customer shall provide samples or photographs.

6.3 **Investigation and Corrective Action.** Supplier shall acknowledge each Nonconformance notice within two (2) business days and, within ten (10) business days, provide Customer with a written root-cause analysis and corrective and preventive action plan. Supplier shall implement the plan within the time agreed with Customer and shall verify its effectiveness.

6.4 **Critical Defects.** If Supplier becomes aware of a Critical Defect in any Lot delivered or about to be delivered to Customer, Supplier shall notify Customer within twenty-four (24) hours and shall place on hold all affected Lots in its possession.

6.5 **Remedies.** Rejected Products are subject to Section 7.2 of the Supply Agreement.

## 7. CHANGE CONTROL

7.1 **Prior Consent.** In accordance with Section 6.3 of the Supply Agreement, Supplier shall not change any raw material, process, mold, facility or Specification affecting the Products without Customer's prior written consent.

7.2 **Change Requests.** Supplier shall submit each proposed change to Customer in writing at least ninety (90) days before the proposed implementation date, together with a description of the change, the reasons for it, an assessment of its effect on the Products, and any validation data.

7.3 **Qualification.** Customer may require Supplier to supply trial quantities of Products made under a proposed change for line trials at Customer's facilities before Customer decides whether to give its consent.

## 8. AUDITS

8.1 **Audit Right.** Customer, or a third-party auditor bound by confidentiality obligations, may audit Supplier's facilities, quality records and systems relating to the Products once in each calendar year on at least fifteen (15) business days' notice, and at any time on reasonable notice following a Critical Defect or a Recall.

8.2 **Findings.** Supplier shall respond in writing to any audit findings within thirty (30) days and shall correct any deficiencies within the time agreed with Customer.

## 9. COMPLAINTS AND RECALLS

9.1 **Consumer Complaints.** Customer shall forward to Supplier any consumer or trade complaint that it reasonably believes relates to the Products. Supplier shall investigate and report its findings within ten (10) business days.

9.2 **Recalls.** Recalls are governed by Section 10 of the Supply Agreement. Supplier shall provide Customer with all traceability records, test data and other information reasonably needed to assess and carry out a Recall within twenty-four (24) hours of Customer's request.

## 10. RECORDS

10.1 **Retention.** Supplier shall keep all production, inspection, testing and release records, CoAs and retained samples for each Lot for at least five (5) years after delivery, consistent with Section 10.3 of the Supply Agreement.

10.2 **Access.** Supplier shall provide copies of these records to Customer on request.

## 11. TERM AND GENERAL

11.1 **Term.** This Quality Agreement takes effect on the Effective Date and continues in effect for as long as the Supply Agreement remains in effect and thereafter for as long as any obligation under Section 10 of this Quality Agreement remains outstanding.

11.2 **Confidentiality.** Information exchanged under this Quality Agreement is Confidential Information subject to Section 12 of the Supply Agreement.

11.3 **Notices.** Notices under this Quality Agreement shall be given in accordance with Section 15.4 of the Supply Agreement. Routine quality communications may be exchanged by email between the Parties' quality representatives.

11.4 **Amendment.** This Quality Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by both Parties, except that Specifications may be updated as provided in Section 2.3.

11.5 **Governing Law and Disputes.** This Quality Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules. Section 15.6 of the Supply Agreement applies to any dispute arising out of or relating to this Quality Agreement.

11.6 **Counterparts.** This Quality Agreement may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature. Each counterpart is an original, and all counterparts together are one instrument.
